3. The facts of the plaint of the aforesaid suit, in brief, are that the suit land belongs to the Government as khas land; that the plaintiffs took settlement of the same for 99 years from the Government vide Settlement Case No. (XII-30/98-99)/(XII-151/95-96) and as such a kabuliyat was registered in their name on 07.12.1999; that since settlement the plaintiffs have been enjoying and possessing the suit land by having the same mutated in their name and also by paying rent to the Government exchequer; that the plaintiffs have their homestead in the suit land and they have been possessing the same since the flood in 1988 by planting different trees; that they did not violate any of the terms of the kabuliyat dated 07.12.1999; that the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Rajbari Sader, Rajbari (defendant No.4) vide his letter dated 12.03.2000 asked the plaintiffs to appear before him for the purpose of hearing in respect of the Kabuliyat and that on his appearance the said defendant threatened to cancel their kabuliyat and hence, the suit. 

 5. The petitioner No.1 as added defendant No.6 contested the suit by filling a separate written statement denying the material facts of the plaint and contending, inter alia, that the suit land originally belonged to Satish Chandra Das, who granted settlement of the same along with other lands in favour of Mohammad Mozahar Ali Miah and Azhar Ali Miah; that in order to recover arrear k rents for 1360-1362 BS from the said tenants Azhar and Mozahar, Satish Chandra filed Rent Suit No.60 of 1957 in the Court of the then Munsif, Goalando and that suit was compromised between the parties on 26.02.1957; that while the said Azhar and 

 Mozahar were enjoying and possessing the land, rent roll record was prepared in their name; that the said Mozahar Hossain transferred his share i.e. 181/2 decimals of land in favour of one Solemannesa by a registered sale deed dated 22.02.1961; that in order to sell the suit land Solemannesa entered into a contract for sale with the defendant-petitioner No.1 on 25.11.1988 fixing the consideration money at Tk.12,000/-; that following the death of Solemannesa her sons, Pran Sheikh and Ramzan Sheikh executed and registered a sale deed in his favour on 16.07.2000; that thereafter on 20.08.2000 the defendant-petitioner No.1 went to the local Tahshil Office to pay rent/land development tax and came to learn that the suit land has been recorded in the name of the Government instead of Solemannesa; that the Government has no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land; that the kabuliyat of the plaintiff's is collusive and ineffective; that the defendant-petitioner No.1 has right, title, interest and possession in the suit land and therefore, the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 6. The predecessor of the petitioner Nos.2-6 as added defendant No.7 also contested the suit by filling another written statement denying the material facts of the plaint and contending, inter alia, that the suit land originally belonged to Satish Chandra Das, who granted settlement of the same along with other lands in favour of Azhar Ali Miah and Mozahar Ali Miah; that in order to recover arrear rents for 1360-1362 BS from the said tenants Azhar and Mozahar, Satish Chandra filed Rent Suit No.60 of 1957 in the Court of the then Munsif, Goalando and that suit was compromised between the parties on 26.02.1957; that pursuant to the said compromise decree, Azhar and Mozahar were admitted as tenants and they remained in possession of the suit land as owner thereof; that Azhar Miah died leaving behind widow Khodeja, 2 sons-Abdul Latif and Golam Sarwar and one daughter Jahanara Begum as his heirs; that the said heirs of Azhar Ali transferred the suit land in favour of the added defendant No.7 by a registered sale deed being No.4239 dated 15.06.1982 and delivered possession in his favour; that the suit land became uncultivable because of situation by the flood of 1988; that the ancestral/paternal residence of the plaintiff's was in Sujanagar, Pabna  and because of destruction of their house in Pabna by a flood in 1988, they stared looking for a piece of land for residential purposes; that the plaintiffs are the distant relatives of the said defendant No.7 and therefore, the latter allowed the former to live in the suit land on a temporary basis given the uncultivable nature of the suit land and accordingly, the plaintiffs erected homestead in the suit land in the first part of 1989 and started living therein and planted various trees; that at that time the plaintiffs undertook to vacate the suit land soon after they get another piece of suitable land; that in the middle of November, 2000 they claimed title to the suit land on the basis of a kabuliyat from the Government and that even being requested to vacate the suit land the plaintiffs refused to do so and as such the said defendant filed Title Suit No.214 of 2000 against the plaintiffs in the Court of the learned Assistant Judge, Rajbari Sader, Rajbari praying for a decree for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession; that the suit land is not at all the khas land of the Government and therefore, the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 On the above point as to the plaintiffs entry into the half portion of the suit land Mr. Bhuiyan submits that form the above-quoted averments made in paragraph 3 of the plaint it is abundantly clear that had the suit land even been vested in the Government as khas land, the same would have been leased out by the Government in favour of any other person/s and in the absence of any such lease it inevitable suggests that the suit land never devolved upon the Government. In this connection Mr. Bhuiyan further submits that the plaintiffs' entered into the suit land in 1988 finding the same as vacant land is nothing but cock and bull story in view of the fact that had the suit land been actually vacant the local people would have taken possession thereof much earlier leaving no room for a stranger coming from a different district called Pabna to occupy the same and erect homestead thereon. 

 20. On the other hand, Mr. Shah Hossain, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-opposite party Nos.1-2 submits that on and from 14` April, 1956 the rent receiving interest of all the rent receivers in Bangladesh having been acquired by the Government under Section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (the SAT Act), the defendant-petitioners' claim of title to the suit land on the strength of a compromise decree dated 26.02.1957 drawn up in Rent Suit No.60 of 1957 between the then Zamindar/landlord Satish Chandra Das and his tenants Mohammad Mozahar Ali Miah and Azhar Ali Miah from whom the petitioners got the suit land by way of successive transfers becomes barred by law. In support of his submission, Mr. Hossain referred to the decisions reported in 31 DLR (AD) 323; 14 BLC 848; 38 DLR (AD) 93 and 20 DLR 699. Amongst the cited decisions, I feel the necessity to quote the ratio decidendi of the case of Government of Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Mymensing vs. Abani Kanta Chakraborty and others 38 DLR (AD) 93, which runs as follows : 

 "After the abolition of all rent receiving interests in the country there is only one class of tenancy under the Government whose rights and liabilities are governed by an uniform law." 

 21. Controverting the above submission readily, Mr. Bhuiyan submits that Rent Suit No.60 of 1957 was filed by the then Zaminder Satish Chandra Das for realizing the arrear rent in respect of the suit land for 1360-1362 BS (corresponding to 1953-1955) and the said Rent Suit having been field within 3 (three) years for realizing the arrear rents for the period before Section 3 of the SAT Act came into force, the said Rent Suit is maintainable within the meaning of Article 110 of the First Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1908 and therefore, the compromise decree drawn up in that suit is legal, whereby the landlord Satish Chandra Das admitted Mozahar Ali and Azhar Ali as his tenants for the period prior to Section 3 of the SAT Act came into force and following the acquisition of the rent receiving interest by the Government, the said tenants Mozahar Ali and Azahar Ali became direct tenants under the Government and the petitioners having acquired title to the suit land by successive transfers by dint of 3(three) separate registered sale deeds of 1961, 1982 and 2000 from them and their transferees, are the lawful title holders of the suit land. 

 25. I have meticulously gone through the revisional application, the impugned judgment and decree, the pleadings of the respective parties, evidence led by them and other materials on record and also heard the learned Advocates for both the sides at length and perused the decisions relied upon by both the parties with utmost circumspection and the relevant provisions of law wherefrom it transpires that the preparation and publication of S.A. record of rights, if any, in the khas khatians of the Government as well as the maintainability of Rent Suit No.60 of 1957 are the predominant issues in this case apart from other connected issues and I will endeavor to address all the issues in proportion to their respective weight and importance.

 28. It appears from Ext.2 of Title Suit No.214 of 2000 (from which Civil Revision No.2748 of 2014 arose and which has been heard and disposed of in simultaneous with the present Rule) that Rent Suit No.60 of 1957 was filed by the then Zaminder Satish Chandra Das against his tenants Mozahar Ali Miah and Azahar Ali Miah for realizing the arrear rent in respect of the suit land for 1360-1362 BS (corresponding to 1953-1955) and the said Rent Suit was filed within 3(three) years for realizing the arrear rents for the period prior to Section 3 of the SAT Act came into force as on 14th April, 1956 and hence, the said Rent Suit is maintainable within the meaning of Article 110 of the First Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1908 and therefore, the compromise decree dated 26.02.1957 (Ext.2 of Title Suit No. 214 of 2000) drawn up in that rent suit is also legal. In this connection I think it would be profitable to quote Article 110 of the First Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1908, which runs as follows: 

 110. For arrears of rent.	Part VI-Three years (cntd) Three years	When the arrears become due 

 It also appears from the abovementioned compromise decree dated 26.02.1957 that landlord Satish Chandra Das admitted Mozahar Ali and Azahar Ali as his tenants for the period prior to Section 3 of the SAT Act came into force and following the acquisition of the rent receiving interest by the Government, the said tenants Mozahar Ali and Azahar Ali became direct tenants under the Government and the petitioners having acquired their title to the suit land by successive transfers by dint of 3(three) separate registered sale deeds dated 01.03.1961 (Ext.2 of Title Suit No.154 of 2000), 15.06.1982 (Ext.5 of Title Suit No.214 of 2000) and 16.07.2000 (Ext.3 of Title Suit No.154 of 2000) from them and their transferees, are the lawful title holders of the suit land. 

 Secondly, it is as clear as broad daylight from R.S. Khatian No.259 (Ext.l of Title Suit No.154 of 2000) that R.S. Plot No.185 is present in the .said khatian showing 37 decimals of land in sixteen annas share. On this point the learned Advocate for the opposite party Nos.1-2 submits that the said finding is merely a slip of pen on the part of the lower appellate Court and in fact the appellate Court below meant R.S. Khatian No.148 (Ext. 1/Ka of Title Suit No.154 of 2000). On scrutiny of R.S. Khatian No.148, it is found that Plot No.285 appears therein, but the quantum of land in the said plot is completely different, namely 15 decimals in eight annas share. Moreover, lands of both the R.S. Khatian being Nos.259 and 148 belonged to Zaminder Satish Chandra Das and as such I find it difficult to accept the submissions advanced from the plaintiffs on this point. Rather, I subscribe to the view that the Court of appeal below wrongly recorded the said finding as to R.S. Khatian No.259 and Plot No.185 upon his total non-application of judicial mind to the materials on record, which is very unbecoming and deplorable on the part of a judicial officer.
